Input image 2 (131): reference ONLY for genuine layered watercolor, luminous pigment and paper; disregard its scene and sharp blush. Match this existing book's painterly visual identity. Broad overlapping translucent watercolor washes visible INSIDE heads, torsos, limbs and hands, gentle pigment pooling, restrained hand-painted texture; no marker, colored-pencil grain, flat vector, glossy/3D paint. Heads are PERFECT CIRCLES, width equals height, no oval, chin, jaw, ears, nose, hair or neck. Medium balanced adult neutral bodies, modest arms, not skinny or chunky; female bodies identical to other bodies, no breast, narrow waist, hip or buttock bulge, indentations. Gender if needed only a few short fine upper-outer eyelashes on the SAME small dark oval eyes. Tiny internal white glints allowed; NO surrounding white sclera. Soft local-color crescent contact shadow under each round head joining shoulders directly. Visible hands have THREE fingers PLUS ONE thumb, normal natural grips. Every foot and important prop fully INSIDE the image, no accidental clipping. Generous irregular watercolor edges with clean white paper margins. All writing ONLY short correctly connected colloquial Persian; no English. Family-friendly, warm, gentle human wit. Read scenes right-to-left then downward, thin WHITE gutters, no heavy frames. Calm uncluttered composition for an ADULT audience, not preschool/chibi.
Three clear scenes: upper RIGHT beginning, upper LEFT middle, wide LOWER result. Small warm restaurant kitchen for adult workers, not toy cooking. PINK head chef and TURQUOISE coworker, both medium neutral adult plain bodies with identical simple straight cream aprons, no hats/hair/shirts. Primary pink has a few subtle short upper outer lashes ONLY; do not curve the hips/waist.
UPPER RIGHT: pink stands comfortably beside prep counter, pointing an impatient order to turquoise, who carries a plainly HEAVY tray stacked with ordinary clean ceramic plates. A small thought bubble above PINK contains just a gold award cup on a pedestal, showing fixation on recognition, not a speech. One short pink speech «زودتر!» Turquoise bends only slightly under load, adult shoulders tense, tired brow, not distorted; all body parts and complete tray fit. No falling plates.
UPPER LEFT: during same busy work, PINK herself now carries that SAME heavy plate tray, both arms visibly supporting it, tired straining eyebrows and weight-bearing stance, feet solidly planted; turquoise works at the sink nearby. She experiences the load rather than showing a silly accident. A small respectful pause and gaze toward coworker make reflection visible; NO moralizing text, no extra thought bubbles.
WIDE LOWER: PINK kindly takes the heavy tray herself from exhausted turquoise, looking at the person, calm concerned smile; turquoise rests hands on a simple counter and gratefully exhales, then helps with a smaller tray. Pink says only «این یکی با من.» She has stopped merely issuing orders and voluntarily shares unpleasant work. The gold-award thought has vanished; no trophy is awarded. fullGenerationPromptEnglish:
Create one finished SQUARE 1:1 narrative watercolor book illustration with THREE scenes. The first scene is at the UPPER RIGHT, the second at the UPPER LEFT, and the result spans the full width of the LOWER HALF. Readers follow right to left across the upper pair, then downward. Use slim clean white gutters, no heavy comic borders, and generous irregular watercolor edges surrounded by white paper. Show two adult restaurant workers in the SAME warm kitchen throughout: a PINK lead cook with a few short fine eyelashes and a TURQUOISE coworker. The pink character initially seeks recognition and impatiently orders the other person, then experiences the same heavy workload, and finally voluntarily takes a share of it. Communicate the change through the repeated stack of plates, expression and action. The illustration is for adults and teenagers, warm and gently witty, never preschool-like or humiliating.

WATERCOLOR AND COLOR
Use genuine hand-painted watercolor on textured white paper, with moderate overlapping translucent washes, luminous light areas, soft natural variation and subtle pigment pooling. Layered paint is clearly visible INSIDE the round heads and all bodies, limbs and hands, as well as in the kitchen. Pink uses rosy, coral and raspberry variations with a restrained darker rose or burgundy contour; turquoise uses cyan and blue variations with a darker blue contour. Body outlines are shades of the body's own color, never black. Facial marks can be small and dark. Use gentle local-color crescent shadows at the head-to-shoulder joins and quiet floor shadows. No flat vector fills, marker strokes, colored-pencil grain, plastic gloss, heavy mottling or 3D rendering. The pale warm tile, gray metal fixtures and cream aprons provide contrast without dulling the body colors. Do not add distinct sharp pink cheek spots; any cheek warmth is a very soft watercolor wash blended into the face. Maintain an airy clean page with all complete people and important objects safely within each scene.

ADULT CHARACTER MODEL
Heads are PERFECT CIRCLES, equal width and height, not ovals. No chin, jaw, nose, ears, hair, hat or separate neck. Heads join directly to the shoulders, with the small watercolor contact shadow distinguishing head from torso. The figures have medium, balanced adult proportions: simple straight or gently rounded neutral torsos, modest arms, adult-length legs and naturally planted rounded feet. Avoid very thin, chubby, bulbous or childlike forms. Pink and turquoise use the same neutral body structure. There are NO breasts, waist pinches, hip or buttock projections or decorative feminine curves. Only a few fine SHORT lashes at the upper outer corners of pink's normal eyes suggest gender. Pink and turquoise both use the same small dark oval eyes, with at most tiny white glints INSIDE them and never white sclera around them. Eyebrows and mouth express effort, impatience, reflection and relief without exaggerated frightening faces. Turquoise may have simple closed happy arc eyes in the final scene. Every hand has THREE fingers PLUS ONE thumb, with realistic tray grips and natural occlusion where the held tray covers fingers. Limbs connect plausibly, and legs align with the standing torso. Both workers wear the SAME simple straight cream work apron, with plain straps, side ties and a rectangular pocket, without other clothing or accessories. Full heads, bodies, legs and BOTH feet of each worker must fit in every scene.

CONTINUOUS KITCHEN
Show a small professional restaurant kitchen rather than a toy kitchen. Pale cream and warm yellow tiles line the walls and floor. Stainless steel work counters, a modest stove with a gently steaming pot, a gray exhaust hood, hanging frying pans, shelves of ordinary stacked white plates and a few metal pots establish the workplace. A compact shelf has a few unlabeled bottles. A work surface or side trolley holds a metal bowl with tomatoes and green herbs; a few wooden utensils stand in a cup. A plain pendant lamp appears near the right work area. The repeated HEAVY stack consists of many ordinary off-white ceramic plates resting flat on the same dark rectangular serving tray. The weight is visible through hands, brow and stance, not through dangerous falling plates. Counters are beside or behind the figures, so they do not hide their legs. All tray edges, table supports and visible floor space fit within the irregular painted boundary. Keep the room believable and visually calm despite its functional details.

UPPER RIGHT, FIRST: AN ORDER DRIVEN BY RECOGNITION
The TURQUOISE coworker stands on the LEFT side of this panel, carrying the heavy tray and tall stack of plates in both hands. The stack sits around chest height. Turquoise takes a small careful step and shows a strained, tired brow, slightly downturned mouth and a couple of small blue effort marks near the head. Do not distort the body or make plates tip over. Both feet and their connected legs are fully visible in the open aisle.
The PINK lead cook stands on the RIGHT beside a metal preparation counter, with feet fully visible. Pink points an impatient arm toward turquoise; the other hand rests near the apron or hip without creating a gendered body contour. The expression has a lowered brow and a small open admonishing mouth. A short speech bubble clearly belonging to pink reads EXACTLY: "زودتر!". Above pink, a separate modest thought cloud contains ONE gold trophy cup on its base with a few warm emphasis marks and NO words. This establishes pink's focus on recognition. The tray, thought cloud and speech bubble are clearly separated. The prep counter is to the side or behind, with complete supports within the frame, never a full-width foreground obstruction.

UPPER LEFT, SECOND: EXPERIENCING THE SAME BURDEN
In the SAME kitchen, PINK now stands on the LEFT and herself supports the SAME heavy tray and stack of plates with both arms. Her full legs and planted feet show a believable weight-bearing stance, medium neutral adult build and a strained worried expression. Add only a few restrained effort marks. She discovers how demanding this ordinary task is; she is not dropping the plates or having a slapstick accident. This is the central causal experience that makes the final action understandable.
The TURQUOISE coworker is on the RIGHT at the sink, washing ordinary dishes with a small yellow sponge and some white soap bubbles. Turquoise's body turns naturally toward the sink while the face remains quietly attentive. Show both complete feet below the apron and sink-side area. Behind them, repeat the hanging pans, steaming pot, shelves and gray fixtures so it is the same work environment. A modest blue dish rack sits low at the right edge, fully inside the panel. There is NO trophy thought cloud, extra dialogue, instructional diagram or written explanation in this scene.

WIDE LOWER SCENE, THIRD: VOLUNTARILY SHARING THE WORK
Open the view enough to show BOTH characters from perfectly circular heads to complete feet, along with the kitchen's side counters and their supports. TURQUOISE stands at the LEFT in the open aisle, now relieved and smiling warmly, with one hand resting on the edge of a LEFT SIDE counter and the other arm relaxed near the apron. Use friendly closed arc eyes and a small open relieved smile, with one tiny unlettered breath puff nearby if useful. The side counter does not hide either leg. Turquoise's stance clearly shows relief from the previous load.
PINK stands toward the RIGHT, carrying the SAME plate tray herself with both arms, now with a calm kind smile and ordinary dark oval eyes. Pink looks toward the coworker as a person rather than at a trophy, and deliberately accepts the unpleasant share of the work. A single speech bubble belongs to pink and reads EXACTLY: "این یکی با من.". Keep the tray heavy and recognizable but level and safely held. Both workers retain identical neutral medium proportions and matching straight cream aprons. There is no trophy, award ceremony, payment or status label in this scene.
The kitchen has an open aisle beneath the characters. The metal counter at the far left contains some plate stacks and a green herb pot, with a tray stored on its lower shelf. On the left rear wall is a small simple dark BLACKBOARD in a wood frame whose surface is COMPLETELY BLANK: no words, heart, doodle or replacement slogan. Repeat the stove, steaming pot, exhaust hood and pan rail behind the figures. At the right are side work surfaces with bowls of vegetables, unlabeled bottles, ordinary stacked dishes and a cup of wooden utensils. The counters' legs stay inside the image. The warm pendant light and tile unify the three scenes without excessive clutter.

TEXT AND FINAL FRAMING
The ONLY written language in the picture is the two quoted short Persian speech lines, naturally connected and legible, in their correct panels and attached to pink. Do not put English, digits, labels, names, signatures, watermarks or a moralizing sentence on any prop or wall. The upper-right order, upper-left experience of carrying the same heavy load, and lower voluntary carrying action must form a clear visual sequence. Keep the mild humor of an impatient boss discovering the weight of the task herself, while maintaining adult dignity. Preserve layered watercolor inside the figures, colored contours, true circular heads, neutral bodies, full feet and ample clean white irregular margins.
